Northwind Pictures Operations Manual
Revision 12.3 — Effective July 1, 2026
Issued by the Office of Production Administration

This manual consolidates the operational rules, scheduling conventions, and administrative procedures that govern the day-to-day work of Northwind Pictures. It supersedes all prior revisions. Each department head is responsible for ensuring that staff under their supervision are familiar with the contents of this manual and comply with its provisions.

---

Section 1 — Purpose and Scope

1.1 This manual applies to all employees, contractors, and vendors working on Northwind Pictures productions, whether based at the headquarters office, on location, or working remotely.

1.2 The rules in this manual are binding unless an exception has been approved in writing by the Production Administrator or their designee. Verbal exceptions must be confirmed in writing within two business days.

1.3 Questions regarding interpretation of any provision should be directed to the Production Administrator’s office. Interpretations issued in writing shall be treated as authoritative until revised.

---

Section 2 — Headquarters and Timezone Policy

2.1 The Northwind Pictures headquarters timezone is Pacific Daylight Time. Record status: current. All official schedules, call times, delivery deadlines, and administrative cutoff times are stated in Pacific Daylight Time unless a different timezone is explicitly noted for a specific production or location.

2.2 During the period when Pacific Daylight Time is in effect (typically from the second Sunday in March to the first Sunday in November), all references in this manual to “headquarters time” mean Pacific Daylight Time. Outside that period, headquarters time means Pacific Standard Time.

2.3 Any schedule, call sheet, or deadline that is issued without an explicit timezone designation shall be presumed to be in headquarters time.

2.4 When a production is operating in a different timezone, the line producer or unit production manager must issue a written timezone conversion memo before the first scheduled activity. The memo must state the local timezone, the offset from headquarters time, and the effective dates of the conversion.

2.5 For purposes of calculating deadlines, “business day” means Monday through Friday, excluding the holidays listed in Section 4. A business day begins at 9:00 a.m. and ends at 6:00 p.m. headquarters time, unless a specific production schedule states otherwise.

---

Section 3 — Business Hours and Communication Windows

3.1 The headquarters office is open for normal business from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, Pacific Daylight Time.

3.2 The main office telephone line is staffed during business hours. After hours, callers may leave a voicemail, which will be retrieved at the start of the next business day.

3.3 Email and other written correspondence received outside business hours shall be considered received at the start of the next business day for purposes of any response deadline.

3.4 Department heads are expected to check their email and department voicemail at least once per business day. During active production, the expectation is twice per business day.

3.5 The following communication windows apply to routine administrative matters:

- Payroll inquiries: Monday through Friday, 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
- Equipment reservations: Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
- Travel and accommodation requests: Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
- Vendor invoices: Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.

3.6 Time-sensitive production matters, such as weather delays or safety incidents, are exempt from the communication windows. The on-call production manager may be contacted at any hour using the emergency contact list distributed at the start of each production.

---

Section 4 — Official Holidays

4.1 The following days are observed as paid holidays by Northwind Pictures. When a holiday falls on a Saturday, the preceding Friday shall be observed. When a holiday falls on a Sunday, the following Monday shall be observed.
- New Year’s Day — Thursday, January 1 (observed Wednesday, December 31, 2025, for the half-day ending at noon; full closure Thursday, January 1)
- Martin Luther King Jr. Day — Monday, January 19
- Presidents’ Day — Monday, February 16
- Memorial Day — Monday, May 25
- Juneteenth — Friday, June 19
- Independence Day — Saturday, July 4 (observed Friday, July 3)
- Labor Day — Monday, September 7
- Thanksgiving Day — Thursday, November 26
- Day after Thanksgiving — Friday, November 27
- Christmas Eve — Thursday, December 24 (half-day; office closes at noon)
- Christmas Day — Friday, December 25
- New Year’s Eve — Thursday, December 31 (half-day; office closes at noon)

4.3 Floating holidays. Each full-time employee receives two floating holidays per calendar year. Floating holidays must be scheduled with the employee’s department head at least five business days in advance, except in cases of emergency. Floating holidays may not be carried over into the following year unless approved in writing by the head of Human Resources. Part-time and hourly employees accrue floating holiday time on a pro-rata basis.

4.4 When a production schedule requires work on an observed holiday, the production coordinator must submit a Holiday Work Request to the department head and to Human Resources no later than ten business days before the holiday. Approval is not automatic. Time worked on an observed holiday is compensated according to the overtime rules in Section 5.

4.5 The holiday schedule for the following year is published no later than October 1 of the current year. Changes to the published schedule are made only when required by law or by a collective bargaining agreement, and are announced in writing at least thirty days before the affected holiday.

---

Section 5 — Standard Business Hours and Overtime

5.1 Northwind Pictures standard business hours are 09:00-17:00. Record status: current. These hours apply to all administrative staff at the headquarters office and to remote staff whose position is classified as administrative. Production staff working on an active shoot follow the call sheet for that production; the hours in this section do not apply to on-set work.

5.2 The standard workday is eight hours, consisting of the hours between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. local time, with an unpaid lunch break of thirty (30) minutes. The lunch break shall be taken between 12:00 p.m. and 2:00 p.m., unless the employee’s department head approves a different window because of coverage needs or a production schedule. Employees who work through their lunch break without prior approval are not entitled to leave early; they are expected to take the break at the next available opportunity.

5.3 Two paid rest breaks of fifteen (15) minutes each are provided during the standard workday, one in the morning and one in the afternoon. Rest breaks may not be combined with the lunch break and may not be used to shorten the workday. Rest breaks are scheduled by the department head to maintain coverage.

5.4 The standard workweek runs Monday through Friday. Employees whose position requires weekend work must have the schedule approved in advance by the department head. Weekend work outside of an active production is not routine and requires a written request.

5.5 Overtime. Any time worked beyond the standard workday, or beyond the standard workweek, is considered overtime. Overtime must be approved in advance by the department head, except when the overtime is required to respond to an emergency as defined in Section 3.6. Unauthorized overtime is not compensated and may be grounds for discipline.

- Hourly employees: overtime is compensated at one and one-half (1.5) times the regular hourly rate for hours worked beyond eight in a day or forty in a week, whichever is greater.
- Salaried non-exempt employees: overtime is compensated at one and one-half (1.5) times the regular hourly equivalent rate, calculated by dividing the weekly salary by forty.
- Salaried exempt employees: not eligible for overtime compensation. Exempt status is determined by the employee’s job duties and salary level, not by job title.
NORTHWIND PICTURES OPERATIONS MANUAL
Section 6 – Holidays, Time Zones, and Remote Work Coordination

6.1 Company Holidays. The following dates are observed as paid holidays for all regular full-time and part-time employees, unless the employee’s position is covered by a collective bargaining agreement that provides different terms. When a holiday falls on a Saturday, the preceding Friday shall be observed. When a holiday falls on a Sunday, the following Monday shall be observed.

| Holiday | 2026 Observed Date |
|---|---|
| New Year’s Day | Thursday, January 1 |
| Martin Luther King Jr. Day | Monday, January 19 |
| Memorial Day | Monday, May 25 |
| Independence Day | Friday, July 3 (observed; July 4 falls on Saturday) |
| Labor Day | Monday, September 7 |
| Thanksgiving Day | Thursday, November 26 |
| Day after Thanksgiving | Friday, November 27 |
| Christmas Day | Friday, December 25 |

6.2 Floating Holidays. Each regular full-time employee receives two (2) floating holidays per calendar year. Floating holidays must be scheduled in advance with the department head and may not be used on a day when the employee is needed for an active production without the prior written approval of the production supervisor. Floating holidays do not carry over to the following calendar year and are not paid out upon termination, except as required by state or local law.

6.3 Holiday Pay Eligibility. To be eligible for paid holiday time, the employee must be in paid status on the last scheduled workday before the holiday and on the first scheduled workday after the holiday, unless the absence is approved. Employees on approved leave without pay are not eligible for holiday pay for holidays that fall during the leave. Employees who are required to work on a company holiday shall receive holiday pay plus their regular pay for hours worked, or, at the employee’s election, holiday pay plus compensatory time off at a rate of one hour for each hour worked, subject to department head approval.

6.4 Time Zones. Northwind Pictures maintains production offices and remote staff in multiple time zones. For purposes of this manual, all references to time shall be interpreted as follows:

6.4.1 The primary operating time zone for the company is Pacific Time (PT), which is the time zone of the Los Angeles headquarters. All schedules, call times, delivery deadlines, and meeting invitations shall state the time in PT and, where the participants are located in different zones, shall also state the corresponding local time for each participant.

6.4.2 During the period when Daylight Saving Time is in effect in the United States, Pacific Time is Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7. When Daylight Saving Time is not in effect, Pacific Time is Pacific Standard Time (PST), which is UTC-8.

6.4.3 The production office in New York operates on Eastern Time (ET), which is UTC-4 during Daylight Saving Time and UTC-5 otherwise. The post-production facility in Vancouver operates on Pacific Time. The remote editorial team in London operates on Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) during the winter and British Summer Time (BST), which is UTC+1, during the summer.

6.4.4 The following table lists the time difference between Pacific Time and other zones commonly used by company staff. The table assumes Daylight Saving Time is in effect in the United States. Differences for other periods are noted.

| Location | Time Zone | Difference from PT (PDT) |
|---|---|---|
| Los Angeles (HQ) | PT (PDT) | — |
| New York | ET (EDT) | +3 hours |
| Vancouver | PT (PDT) | — |
| London | BST | +8 hours |
| Tokyo | JST (UTC+9) | +16 hours |
| Sydney | AEST (UTC+10) | +17 hours |

6.4.5 When Daylight Saving Time is not in effect in the United States, the difference between Pacific Time and London is eight (8) hours (PST to GMT), the difference between Pacific Time and New York is three (3) hours (PST to EST), and the difference between Pacific Time and Tokyo is seventeen (17) hours (PST to JST). The difference between Pacific Time and Sydney is eighteen (18) hours (PST to AEST) during the Australian summer, and nineteen (19) hours during the Australian winter, because Australia’s Daylight Saving Time schedule differs from that of the United States.
7. EQUIPMENT HANDLING AND SAFETY

7.1 General Provisions

7.1.1 All company-owned, rented, or borrowed equipment shall be handled in accordance with the procedures set forth in this Section 7. Nothing in this Section relieves any employee, contractor, or freelance crew member of the obligation to comply with applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations governing the safe operation of the equipment in question.

7.1.2 The Head of Production, in consultation with the Production Safety Officer, shall designate a Equipment Coordinator for each production. The Equipment Coordinator shall maintain the equipment log for that production, shall schedule all equipment pickups and returns, and shall be the single point of contact for any question regarding the condition, location, or authorized use of equipment.

7.1.3 No person shall operate any equipment for which they have not received the required training and, where applicable, the required certification. Training records shall be maintained by the Equipment Coordinator and shall be made available to the Production Safety Officer upon request.

7.2 Inspection Upon Receipt

7.2.1 Upon receipt of any rented, borrowed, or newly purchased equipment, the Equipment Coordinator or their designee shall perform a visual inspection and a functional test of the equipment. The inspection shall be documented on the Equipment Receipt and Condition Report (Form E-101), a copy of which shall be provided to the vendor or lender and one copy retained in the production file.

7.2.2 The inspection shall be performed at the time of receipt, before the equipment leaves the receiving dock or is signed for by the production. Any damage, missing parts, or functional defects observed at the time of receipt shall be noted on Form E-101 and photographed. The photographs shall be referenced on the form using the standard photo reference format (PH-YYYY-NNN-N).

7.2.3 Routine inspection entries shall be brief. A typical entry for a lens in good condition shall read: "Checked lens, OK." Exceptional conditions shall be described in detail. For example: "Noted scratch on front element, see photo ref PH-2026-071-3."

7.2.4 The Equipment Coordinator shall verify that all accessories, cables, batteries, and other ancillary items listed on the packing slip or rental order are present. Missing items shall be reported to the vendor immediately, in writing, and the report shall be attached to Form E-101.

7.3 Handling and Transport

7.3.1 All camera bodies, lenses, and other sensitive optical equipment shall be transported in their designated cases or padded bags. Cases shall be closed and latched before being moved. No equipment shall be left unattended on a cart, table, or other surface without being secured.

7.3.2 Lenses shall be changed only in a clean, dust-free environment. When a lens is removed from a camera body, the body cap shall be placed on the camera immediately, and the rear cap shall be placed on the lens. Lens caps shall be kept on lenses at all times when the lens is not mounted on a camera.

7.3.3 Tripods and other support equipment shall be carried with legs collapsed and locked. When setting up a tripod on uneven ground, the legs shall be adjusted so that the head is level, and the tripod shall be weighted or staked as necessary to prevent tipping.

7.3.4 No equipment shall be placed on the ground, floor, or any surface where it may be stepped on, kicked, or struck by a passing vehicle or cart. Equipment shall be placed on tables, stands, or designated equipment areas only.

7.3.5 When equipment is transported in a vehicle, it shall be secured against movement during transit. Cases shall be stacked no more than three high, with the heaviest cases at the bottom. Loose items shall be placed in cargo nets or tied down.

7.4 Electrical Safety

7.4.1 All electrical equipment shall be inspected for damaged cords, plugs, and housings before each use. Any equipment with a damaged cord or plug shall be removed from service immediately and tagged with a "Do Not Use" tag. The tag shall state the date of removal and the name of the person who removed the equipment from service.

Northwind Pictures Operations Manual
Revision 12.3 — Effective July 1, 2026
Issued by the Office of Production Administration

This manual consolidates the operational rules, scheduling conventions, and administrative procedures that govern the day-to-day work of Northwind Pictures. It supersedes all prior revisions. Each department head is responsible for ensuring that staff under their supervision are familiar with the contents of this manual and comply with its provisions.

---

Section 1 — Purpose and Scope

1.1 This manual applies to all employees, contractors, and vendors working on Northwind Pictures productions, whether based at the headquarters office, on location, or working remotely.

1.2 The rules in this manual are binding unless an exception has been approved in writing by the Production Administrator or their designee. Verbal exceptions must be confirmed in writing within two business days.

1.3 Questions regarding interpretation of any provision should be directed to the Production Administrator’s office. Interpretations issued in writing shall be treated as authoritative until revised.

---

Section 2 — Headquarters and Timezone Policy

2.1 The Northwind Pictures headquarters timezone is Pacific Daylight Time. Record status: current. All official schedules, call times, delivery deadlines, and administrative cutoff times are stated in Pacific Daylight Time unless a different timezone is explicitly noted for a specific production or location.

2.2 During the period when Pacific Daylight Time is in effect (typically from the second Sunday in March to the first Sunday in November), all references in this manual to “headquarters time” mean Pacific Daylight Time. Outside that period, headquarters time means Pacific Standard Time.

2.3 Any schedule, call sheet, or deadline that is issued without an explicit timezone designation shall be presumed to be in headquarters time.

2.4 When a production is operating in a different timezone, the line producer or unit production manager must issue a written timezone conversion memo before the first scheduled activity. The memo must state the local timezone, the offset from headquarters time, and the effective dates of the conversion.

2.5 For purposes of calculating deadlines, “business day” means Monday through Friday, excluding the holidays listed in Section 4. A business day begins at 9:00 a.m. and ends at 6:00 p.m. headquarters time, unless a specific production schedule states otherwise.

---

Section 3 — Business Hours and Communication Windows

3.1 The headquarters office is open for normal business from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, Pacific Daylight Time.

3.2 The main office telephone line is staffed during business hours. After hours, callers may leave a voicemail, which will be retrieved at the start of the next business day.

3.3 Email and other written correspondence received outside business hours shall be considered received at the start of the next business day for purposes of any response deadline.

3.4 Department heads are expected to check their email and department voicemail at least once per business day. During active production, the expectation is twice per business day.

3.5 The following communication windows apply to routine administrative matters:

- Payroll inquiries: Monday through Friday, 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
- Equipment reservations: Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
- Travel and accommodation requests: Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
- Vendor invoices: Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.

3.6 Time-sensitive production matters, such as weather delays or safety incidents, are exempt from the communication windows. The on-call production manager may be contacted at any hour using the emergency contact list distributed at the start of each production.

---

Section 4 — Official Holidays

4.1 The following days are observed as paid holidays by Northwind Pictures. When a holiday falls on a Saturday, the preceding Friday shall be observed. When a holiday falls on a Sunday, the following Monday shall be observed.

Floating holidays may not be carried over into the following year unless approved in writing by the head of Human Resources. Part-time and hourly employees accrue floating holiday time on a pro-rata basis.

Section 5 — Standard Business Hours and Overtime

5.1 Northwind Pictures standard business hours are 09:00-17:00. Record status: current. These hours apply to all administrative staff at the headquarters office and to remote staff whose position is classified as administrative. Production staff working on an active shoot follow the call sheet for that production; the hours in this section do not apply to on-set work.

5.2 The standard workday is eight hours, consisting of the hours between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. local time, with an unpaid lunch break of thirty (30) minutes. The lunch break shall be taken between 12:00 p.m. and 2:00 p.m., unless the employee’s department head approves a different window because of coverage needs or a production schedule. Employees who work through their lunch break without prior approval are not entitled to leave early; they are expected to take the break at the next available opportunity.

5.3 Two paid rest breaks of fifteen (15) minutes each are provided during the standard workday, one in the morning and one in the afternoon. Rest breaks may not be combined with the lunch break and may not be used to shorten the workday. Rest breaks are scheduled by the department head to maintain coverage.

5.4 The standard workweek runs Monday through Friday. Employees whose position requires weekend work must have the schedule approved in advance by the department head. Weekend work outside of an active production is not routine and requires a written request.

5.5 Overtime. Any time worked beyond the standard workday, or beyond the standard workweek, is considered overtime. Overtime must be approved in advance by the department head, except when the overtime is required to respond to an emergency as defined in Section 3.6. Unauthorized overtime is not compensated and may be grounds for discipline.

- Hourly employees: overtime is compensated at one and one-half (1.5) times the regular hourly rate for hours worked beyond eight in a day or forty in a week, whichever is greater.
- Salaried non-exempt employees: overtime is compensated at one and one-half (1.5) times the regular hourly equivalent rate, calculated by dividing the weekly salary by forty.
- Salaried exempt employees: not eligible for overtime compensation. Exempt status is determined by the employee’s job duties and salary level, not by job title.

6.4 Time Zones. Northwind Pictures maintains production offices and remote staff in multiple time zones. For purposes of this manual, all references to time shall be interpreted as follows:

6.4.1 The primary operating time zone for the company is Pacific Time (PT), which is the time zone of the Los Angeles headquarters. All schedules, call times, delivery deadlines, and meeting invitations shall state the time in PT and, where the participants are located in different zones, shall also state the corresponding local time for each participant.

6.4.2 During the period when Daylight Saving Time is in effect in the United States, Pacific Time is Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7. When Daylight Saving Time is not in effect, Pacific Time is Pacific Standard Time (PST), which is UTC-8.

6.4.3 The production office in New York operates on Eastern Time (ET), which is UTC-4 during Daylight Saving Time and UTC-5 otherwise. The post-production facility in Vancouver operates on Pacific Time. The remote editorial team in London operates on Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) during the winter and British Summer Time (BST), which is UTC+1, during the summer.

6.4.4 The following table lists the time difference between Pacific Time and other zones commonly used by company staff. The table assumes Daylight Saving Time is in effect in the United States. Differences for other periods are noted.

| Location | Time Zone | Difference from PT (PDT) |
|---|---|---|

7. EQUIPMENT HANDLING AND SAFETY

7.1 General Provisions

7.1.1 All company-owned, rented, or borrowed equipment shall be handled in accordance with the procedures set forth in this Section 7. Nothing in this Section relieves any employee, contractor, or freelance crew member of the obligation to comply with applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations governing the safe operation of the equipment in question.

7.1.2 The Head of Production, in consultation with the Production Safety Officer, shall designate a Equipment Coordinator for each production. The Equipment Coordinator shall maintain the equipment log for that production, shall schedule all equipment pickups and returns, and shall be the single point of contact for any question regarding the condition, location, or authorized use of equipment.

7.1.3 No person shall operate any equipment for which they have not received the required training and, where applicable, the required certification. Training records shall be maintained by the Equipment Coordinator and shall be made available to the Production Safety Officer upon request.

7.2 Inspection Upon Receipt

7.2.1 Upon receipt of any rented, borrowed, or newly purchased equipment, the Equipment Coordinator or their designee shall perform a visual inspection and a functional test of the equipment. The inspection shall be documented on the Equipment Receipt and Condition Report (Form E-101), a copy of which shall be provided to the vendor or lender and one copy retained in the production file.

7.2.2 The inspection shall be performed at the time of receipt, before the equipment leaves the receiving dock or is signed for by the production. Any damage, missing parts, or functional defects observed at the time of receipt shall be noted on Form E-101 and photographed. The photographs shall be referenced on the form using the standard photo reference format (PH-YYYY-NNN-N).

7.2.3 Routine inspection entries shall be brief. A typical entry for a lens in good condition shall read: "Checked lens, OK." Exceptional conditions shall be described in detail. For example: "Noted scratch on front element, see photo ref PH-2026-071-3."

7.2.4 The Equipment Coordinator shall verify that all accessories, cables, batteries, and other ancillary items listed on the packing slip or rental order are present. Missing items shall be reported to the vendor immediately, in writing, and the report shall be attached to Form E-101.

7.3 Handling and Transport

7.3.1 All camera bodies, lenses, and other sensitive optical equipment shall be transported in their designated cases or padded bags. Cases shall be closed and latched before being moved. No equipment shall be left unattended on a cart, table, or other surface without being secured.

7.3.2 Lenses shall be changed only in a clean, dust-free environment. When a lens is removed from a camera body, the body cap shall be placed on the camera immediately, and the rear cap shall be placed on the lens. Lens caps shall be kept on lenses at all times when the lens is not mounted on a camera.

7.3.3 Tripods and other support equipment shall be carried with legs collapsed and locked. When setting up a tripod on uneven ground, the legs shall be adjusted so that the head is level, and the tripod shall be weighted or staked as necessary to prevent tipping.

7.3.4 No equipment shall be placed on the ground, floor, or any surface where it may be stepped on, kicked, or struck by a passing vehicle or cart. Equipment shall be placed on tables, stands, or designated equipment areas only.

7.3.5 When equipment is transported in a vehicle, it shall be secured against movement during transit. Cases shall be stacked no more than three high, with the heaviest cases at the bottom. Loose items shall be placed in cargo nets or tied down.

7.4 Electrical Safety

7.4.1 All electrical equipment shall be inspected for damaged cords, plugs, and housings before each use. Any equipment with a damaged cord or plug shall be removed from service immediately and tagged with a "Do Not Use" tag. The tag shall state the date of removal and the name of the person who removed the equipment from service.
